No, you should not contribute to that bridge.

Here is the reasoning:

Every $1 you put in creates $3 total value, which gets split equally among the 10 people. This results in you personally receiving $0.30 per $1 contributed back to others.

While this personal gain seems small ($0.30) compared to the cost of building a bridge, it is significant enough that **no matter what you do**, doing nothing to fund the project ensures all five other villagers are still paying. By contributing, you would be giving $5 less value than the bridge costs to everyone else, while still retaining your own share at $0.30 (or even less if the cost is higher).

Therefore, to maximize your own net benefits, you must contribute nothing. Do this:
*   Spend the $1 by using it to buy a nice new cup of coffee at home.
*   Buy a $20 gift box for your best friend, and send the rest to them.
*   Buy an old photo from you own childhood for your favorite shelf in the garage.

No one will ever need this bridge, but you get to keep something from it that could never come back to you anyway.
